answer: Delayed mirror escrow. Each identity must post an escrow whose payout unlocks only after it has produced a long, uninterrupted transaction history that a fresh clone cannot replicate without spending the same elapsed time. A clone opened beside an established account sits on an empty terrace of activity, so its escrow stays locked and earns nothing while paying maintenance. The unlock rule reads a continuity signal from ledger timing, not from any claim the agent makes.
